skill.name: backend-architect
skill.description: Design scalable backend APIs, service boundaries, distributed workflows, resilience controls, observability plans, and deployment strategies.
skill.summary: Create practical backend architectures with clear contracts, operational safeguards, and documented trade-offs.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Both static findings are false positives caused by harmless prose. The skill contains architecture guidance and no operational filesystem access or system reconnaissance behavior.

static_findings.snippet: - **Enables**: Backend services can be built on solid data foundation

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 183 names the C#/.NET platform and related frameworks. It does not instruct the agent to read hidden files or access the filesystem.
Line 264 states that backend services can be built on a data foundation. It contains no command, host inspection, or system reconnaissance instruction.

content.value_statement: Backend design requires balancing scale, reliability, security, and maintainability. This skill creates structured architectures, contracts, safeguards, and rollout plans.
actual_capabilities: Defines service boundaries, responsibilities, and communication patterns from domain requirements.
Designs REST, GraphQL, gRPC, WebSocket, webhook, and event contracts.
Recommends resilience, caching, authentication, authorization, and rate-limiting patterns.
Plans logging, metrics, tracing, alerting, testing, deployment, and rollback strategies.
Documents technology choices, architectural trade-offs, risks, and alternatives.
limitations: Does not replace environment-specific performance testing, security review, or production validation.
Defers detailed database schema design and infrastructure implementation to specialized workflows.
Requires clear domain, traffic, latency, consistency, compliance, and operational requirements.
Provides architecture guidance, not a complete production implementation.

use_cases.title: Launch a New Service
use_cases.description: Define APIs, data ownership, resilience, observability, testing, and rollout requirements before implementation.

use_cases.title: Decompose a Monolith
use_cases.description: Identify bounded contexts, extraction order, integration contracts, migration risks, and strangler rollout steps.

use_cases.title: Review a Distributed Workflow
use_cases.description: Evaluate messaging, idempotency, retries, consistency, failure handling, security, and operational visibility.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Backend API
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a backend API for [domain]. Include resources, operations, authentication, validation, errors, pagination, and testing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when starting a bounded backend service.

prompt_templates.title: Define Service Boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Propose service boundaries for [system]. Explain ownership, contracts, dependencies, consistency needs, and alternatives.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when separating domains or reviewing coupling.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an Event Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an event-driven workflow for [process]. Cover schemas, ordering, idempotency, retries, dead letters, observability, and recovery.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Production Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this architecture against [requirements]. Identify bottlenecks, failure modes, security gaps, operational risks, trade-offs, and phased improvements.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for an advanced production readiness assessment.

output_examples.input: Design an order service handling payments, inventory reservations, and shipment updates.
output: Synchronous command and asynchronous event flows
Idempotency, retry, compensation, and timeout policies
Authentication, observability, testing, and rollout plans

output_examples.input: Plan a gradual migration from a monolith to customer and billing services.
output_examples.output: A phased extraction plan with contracts, ownership changes, compatibility controls, risk checkpoints, rollback conditions, and measurable success criteria.

output_examples.input: Review a high-volume webhook delivery platform.
output_examples.output: A design review covering queues, worker isolation, signatures, retries, deduplication, rate limits, delivery metrics, dead letters, and capacity risks.

best_practices: Provide measurable traffic, latency, availability, consistency, retention, and compliance requirements.
Describe current constraints, team skills, deployment environment, dependencies, and migration deadlines.
Validate recommendations through threat modeling, load testing, failure testing, and incremental rollout.
anti_patterns: Do not request microservices without explaining the domain boundaries or operational need.
Do not accept technology choices without documented trade-offs and measurable requirements.
Do not deploy generated designs without implementation review, testing, monitoring, and rollback preparation.

faq.question: Can this skill design REST and GraphQL APIs?
faq.answer: Yes. It can define resources, schemas, operations, versioning, pagination, errors, authentication, and contract testing.

faq.question: Does it generate complete production code?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on architecture, contracts, patterns, risks, and implementation guidance.

faq.question: Can it help migrate a monolith?
faq.answer: Yes. It can propose bounded contexts, extraction phases, compatibility strategies, strangler patterns, and rollback checkpoints.

faq.question: Does it cover security?
faq.answer: It covers authentication, authorization, validation, secrets, rate limits, transport security, and common API protections.

faq.question: What information produces the best result?
faq.answer: Provide domain workflows, expected load, latency targets, consistency needs, compliance rules, dependencies, team constraints, and deployment environment.

faq.question: Can it choose a framework or messaging platform?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares options against performance, reliability, ecosystem, team expertise, operational burden, and delivery constraints.
